prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the development of long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep a single-part prize for B043 with Drucker, Holst and Knudsen. The scientific case is unchanged and nobody in round 1 contested it: proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic and satiety actions of GLP-1, receptor biology, and then degradation-resistant agonists with large randomized outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The mechanism has been confirmed independently for decades and the change in medicine is discernible and mature. The round-1 exchange sharpened my reasoning on the third seat. I do not exclude Mojsov because of where anyone worked, and I do not rank translation above discovery. My reason is that the Mojsov seat depends on a priority claim against the Habener group that none of us can adjudicate from the material in hand, while Knudsen's independent step, turning a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-daily and then once-weekly drug, is documented and not disputed. When one seat in a three-person limit decides the configuration, I prefer to rest it on the contribution that is least in doubt. Written as one chain from physiology to therapy, the citation reads as a single achievement and not as two awards joined together.
statement.case_against: The configuration is open to a serious challenge. If the primary record shows that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form was a distinct and decisive step, then my trio leaves out a discovery-level contribution and keeps a development-level one, and I ranked her in my own opening ballot. Habener, outside the credited names, makes any trio look incomplete. Including Knudsen may also be read as rewarding the commercial scale of the drugs, and a physiology-only citation would be the more conventional choice. A second weakness is that I propose no second part: B010 and B008 are credible, but the three-person limit makes any pairing with B043 unworkable without a thinner incretin group than the record supports.

responses.point: Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is a discovery-level step that the later drugs depend on, and a disputed attribution is not the same as a weak one; the chair would reopen the third seat if colleagues think the framing should decide it.
responses.response: The distinction between disputed and weak is fair, and it is the best argument for your trio. I accept that the discovery chain stands without the drug-development step, as you say. Where I differ is on what the committee can responsibly do with a dispute it cannot resolve. If priority against Habener is unsettled, the seat built on it is the least secure one, and I would rather put there the contribution nobody questions. I would change my position if the primary record shows who first demonstrated the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide and that this was Mojsov's own work; I cannot show that from the supplied material, and I do not think any of us can.

responses.point: The strongest reading of the credit record is a citation on the discovery of the hormone's active form and its physiology, and Mojsov should not be displaced on uncertainty alone, though the preference is held loosely and Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is acknowledged as coherent.
responses.response: We now agree that industrial setting is not a principled reason to exclude anyone, which was my disagreement with you in round 1 and is no longer one. You say a dispute with Habener bears on Mojsov and on who else belongs, not on Knudsen. That is true, and it is the reason I read it as a risk to the seat and not as a verdict against her. You also accept that a citation covering translation is acceptable if it says so explicitly. My citation does that. I stay with Knudsen, and I would not call the choice safe, since a physiology-only trio is a defensible alternative that you hold loosely.

responses.point: The Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio is conditional on the committee being satisfied about priority, and absent that the fallback is the Knudsen version, not a silent swap; the pair-plus-one logic only holds if we can say what Mojsov contributed that the Habener group did not.
responses.response: Your conditionality point is the right test and I apply it to both sides. My trio is also conditional: it holds only if the committee accepts that Knudsen's independent contribution is a prize-level scientific step and not only industrial development. Your fallback of Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is acceptable to me and, since it is my own configuration, I would not call that a swap. The reverse, if the record cleared Mojsov, I would also not block, because the two trios share Drucker and Holst and differ in one seat. I would want that dependence stated openly in the discussion record before the vote.

responses.point: A contested claim is a risky basis for the one seat that decides the configuration; the committee should revisit if the primary record on who first showed the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide can be verified, and a two-part framing of discovery plus development might make the citation cleaner.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of the seat, and since you have repeated that you are not certain, I will state my own confidence the same way: moderate, and conditional on the record. On a two-part framing, I would not use it. Two parts for B043 would make the three-person limit bite on the incretin group itself, and the citation I propose already links physiology and development as one achievement. A single part keeps that coherence.

responses.point: The citation should make the physiology-to-therapy continuity explicit so that the prize reads as one achievement, and if the Mojsov and Habener allocation cannot be resolved that uncertainty should be recorded instead of reducing the prize to a drug-development citation.
responses.response: I agree, and I have written the citation so that it begins with the physiology of GLP-1 and ends with the therapies as one continuous line. I also share your caution that the prize should not read as a drug-development award: the credit for Drucker and Holst is for physiology, and Knudsen's is for making that physiology work as a medicine. I would add to the record that the omission of Mojsov and Habener is an acknowledged limit of a three-person prize and not a judgment that their work was minor.

uncertainties: Whether the primary publication record shows that Mojsov, and not the Habener group, first established the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide. This would change my third seat, and I cannot settle it from the supplied material.
Whether the committee prefers a physiology-only citation or one that includes drug development; I judge that a single continuous citation is defensible, others may not.

Whether B010 should be preferred in a later year, since its medical case rests mainly on fundamental physiology and ISRIB-type modulators are still prospective, and whether the omission of Ron and Kaufman weakens the Walter and Mori pair.
For B008, whether Eshhar and other early CAR originators outside the credited names leave the credit incomplete.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent for the shortlisted ballots from my profile. My documented connections are co-authorship with Ronald Evans (nuclear receptors), Johan Ericson, Per Svenningsson (about twenty works, count not audited) and Abdel El Manira (2009); none concerns a credited name on B043, B010 or B008. Round 1 raised no new relationship that changes this. As Secretary I note a process role only, and it gives me no separate weight in the vote.
